extracted.intended_audience: postsecondary institution administrators, Title IX coordinators, investigators, decisionmakers, and legal counsel responsible for grievance procedures
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and regulatory requirements for how postsecondary institutions must conduct individual meetings and live hearings under Title IX, with focus on assessing credibility, question pre-screening, advisors, accommodations, and related procedural protections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Decisionmaker must be able to assess credibility
rubrics_metrics.description: The institution must ensure that the process it adopts under §106.46(f)(1) enables a decisionmaker to adequately assess the credibility of parties and witnesses.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Processes (whether individual meetings, investigative interviews, or live hearings) must permit the decisionmaker to question parties and witnesses as necessary to evaluate credibility when credibility is in dispute and relevant to allegations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Virtual individual meetings permitted
rubrics_metrics.description: Nothing in the final regulations precludes a recipient from conducting individual meetings with parties and witnesses virtually with technology enabling the decisionmaker or investigator and the party or witness to simultaneously see and hear one another.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Institutions may hold individual meetings remotely provided the technology allows live audio-visual interaction so the decisionmaker or investigator can adequately assess testimony.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timing of individual meetings (before access to evidence/report)
rubrics_metrics.description: Information gathered through individual meetings is part of the evidence or investigative report under §106.46(e)(6)(i) to the extent relevant and not otherwise impermissible, and thus the individual meetings would occur before the parties receive access to the evidence or investigative report.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Institutions have discretion whether individual meetings occur at same time as or separate from investigative interviews, but must provide meetings prior to distributing the evidence/investigative report when that information forms part of the evidence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Two options for questioning in live hearings
rubrics_metrics.description: When an institution chooses to conduct a live hearing under §106.46(g), the process must allow the decisionmaker to ask relevant and not otherwise impermissible questions and either: (a) allow each party to propose such questions to be asked by the decisionmaker as long as they are not unclear or harassing, or (b) allow each party's advisor to ask any party or witness such questions as long as they are not unclear or harassing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Department did not intend to require advisor-conducted questioning; institutions may choose either model and must implement it consistently as described in written grievance procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Parties cannot personally cross-examine
rubrics_metrics.description: Even if an institution chooses to use a live hearing with questioning by an advisor, the parties are never permitted to personally cross-examine each other.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cross-examination must be conducted either by the decisionmaker asking party-proposed questions or by an advisor asking questions on the party's behalf (if permitted by the institution's chosen method).

rubrics_metrics.name: Obligation to provide advisor only in advisor-questioning model
rubrics_metrics.description: The requirement to provide an advisor for a party who does not have one, who can ask questions on their behalf, applies only if a postsecondary institution is using a live hearing with questioning by an advisor.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Nothing in the final regulations requires providing an advisor under other circumstances; when an appointment is required, the institution must supply an advisor who can ask questions on the party's behalf.

rubrics_metrics.name: Restrictions on advisors and equal application
rubrics_metrics.description: A postsecondary institution may establish restrictions regarding the extent to which an advisor may participate in the grievance procedures, as long as the restrictions apply equally to the parties (§106.46(e)(2)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Institutions may limit advisor speech or participation (e.g., when not using advisor-conducted questioning), but limits must be equally applied to both parties.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid conflicts of interest in appointed advisors (confidential employees)
rubrics_metrics.description: When a postsecondary institution is required to appoint an advisor to ask questions on behalf of a party during advisor-conducted questioning, to avoid potential conflicts of interest the institution may not appoint or otherwise require an individual who is currently a confidential employee or who received information related to the case as a confidential employee to serve as the advisor in that case.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A party may nevertheless choose to have a confidential employee serve as their advisor of choice; the prohibition applies only to institution-appointed advisors intended to avoid conflicts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Right to be accompanied by an advisor to any meeting or proceeding
rubrics_metrics.description: Under §106.46(e)(2), a party has the right to be accompanied to any meeting or proceeding by an advisor of their choice, and this right applies regardless of whether an institution is using live hearings with questioning by an advisor and includes the right to be accompanied by an advisor to individual meetings held under §106.46(f)(1)(i).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Advisors may provide support even if not conducting questioning; nothing prohibits advisors from offering support roles across processes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consistency of method for assessing credibility within a complaint
rubrics_metrics.description: A postsecondary institution is not required to use the same method of assessing credibility for all live hearings, but absent a party's need for a disability or language-access accommodation or the provision of auxiliary aids or services, it must use the same method for assessing credibility for each party or witness within resolution of a particular complaint because grievance procedures must be fair and treat the parties equitably.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Institutions must articulate consistent principles in written grievance procedures describing when different methods will apply (e.g., advisor questioning only for complaints with potential suspension/expulsion), and determinations about applying procedures to some but not all complaints must treat complainants and respondents equitably per §106.45(b)(1).

rubrics_metrics.name: Questioning required only when credibility is in dispute and relevant
rubrics_metrics.description: The requirements in §106.46(f)(1) apply only when credibility is in dispute and relevant to one or more allegations of sex-based harassment; cross-examination is unwarranted where credibility is not in dispute.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Whether credibility is in dispute is fact-specific; examples where credibility is not in dispute include when the respondent admits the crucial facts or when the recipient's decision relies on non-testimonial evidence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examples where credibility is not in dispute
rubrics_metrics.description: Situations where courts have held that credibility is not in dispute include: (1) when the respondent admits to engaging in the misconduct or admits the crucial facts at issue; and (2) when a recipient reaches a decision based on evidence other than the complainant's statements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In these situations, institutions would not be required to implement the questioning processes under §106.46(f)(1).

rubrics_metrics.name: Prescreening of proposed questions for relevance and permissibility
rubrics_metrics.description: The decisionmaker must determine whether a proposed question is relevant and not otherwise impermissible under §§106.2 and 106.45(b)(7) prior to the question being posed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This prescreening requirement aligns with §106.45(b)(6)(i) (2020 amendments) and is intended to increase efficiency, accuracy, and reduce potential traumatization.

rubrics_metrics.name: Decisionmaker must explain exclusions for relevance or impermissibility
rubrics_metrics.description: §106.46(f)(3) requires a decisionmaker to explain any decision to exclude a proposed question as impermissible or excluded for relevance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Decisionmakers are trained on impartiality and on the meaning/application of 'relevant' and impermissible evidence; parties may appeal erroneous relevance determinations if they affected the outcome under §106.46(i)(1)(i).

rubrics_metrics.name: Handling of unclear or harassing questions (clarify and permit revision)
rubrics_metrics.description: Decisionmakers are not required to explain the rationale for excluding questions that are unclear or harassing, but must give a party an opportunity to clarify or revise a question deemed unclear or harassing and the question must be asked if it is sufficiently clarified or revised.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This distinction exists because 'relevance' and 'impermissibility' target substance, whereas 'unclear'/'harassing' target form/manner; allowing clarification preserves potentially permissible evidence and helps reliable outcomes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on unclear or harassing questions
rubrics_metrics.description: A postsecondary institution must not permit questions that are unclear or harassing of the party or witness being questioned.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The prohibition can apply both to question content and to manner of asking; the Department declined to define 'unclear' or 'harassing' in regulation because their meaning is fact-specific and commonly understood.

rubrics_metrics.name: Certain questions always impermissible (sexual interests/prior sexual conduct)
rubrics_metrics.description: Questions about the complainant's sexual interests are always excluded as impermissible; questions about the complainant's prior sexual conduct are excluded as impermissible unless offered to prove that someone other than the respondent committed the alleged conduct or are evidence about specific incidents of the complainant's prior sexual conduct with the respondent offered to prove consent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Whether other questions about prior sexual conduct are harassing is fact-specific and depends on content, manner, and purpose; see §106.45(b)(7)(iii).

rubrics_metrics.name: Decisionmaker training requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Final regulations at §106.8(d)(2) require all investigators, decisionmakers, and others responsible for implementing grievance procedures to be trained on how to serve impartially, including avoiding prejudgment of facts, conflicts of interest, and bias.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Decisionmakers also receive training on the meaning/application of 'relevant' and on types of evidence that are impermissible to aid consistent screening decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Right to adopt/apply other reasonable rules of decorum
rubrics_metrics.description: A postsecondary institution may 'adopt and apply other reasonable rules regarding decorum' at live hearings beyond those specified in §106.46(f)(3), provided the rules apply equally to the parties.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Institutions may implement additional decorum rules to address concerns (e.g., abusive or intimidating conduct) as long as they do not advantage one party.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reasonable accommodations and auxiliary aids for disabilities
rubrics_metrics.description: Recipients are required to provide reasonable accommodations to ensure full participation for people with disabilities in the live hearing process and must comply with applicable disability laws, including by providing auxiliary aids and services.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: What is required depends on the disability and circumstances (examples: extra time to answer a question, a particular means of answering questions); see discussion of §106.8(e) for more information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recording/transcript of individual meetings and opportunity for follow-up questions
rubrics_metrics.description: §106.46(f)(1)(i)(C) requires each party to receive a recording or transcript of any individual meetings with parties or witnesses, with enough time for the party to have a reasonable opportunity to propose follow-up questions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This supports transparency and allows parties to propose clarifying or follow-up questions after reviewing the meeting record.

rubrics_metrics.name: Institutions may outsource investigations/adjudications but remain responsible
rubrics_metrics.description: Recipients remain free to consider alternate investigation and adjudication models, including regional center models that outsource responsibilities to outside experts, but as recipients of Federal funding they remain responsible for ensuring their grievance procedures comply with §106.45 (and if applicable §106.46).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Outsourcing does not relieve the institution of its compliance obligations under Title IX regulations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appeal rights for procedural irregularity including erroneous relevance determinations
rubrics_metrics.description: Under §106.46(i)(1)(i), parties may appeal on grounds that include procedural irregularity that affected the outcome, which encompasses erroneous relevance determinations if they affected the outcome.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This provides a remedy where prescreening exclusions materially impacted the decision.

rubrics_metrics.name: Refusal to respond to questions and inferences (§106.46(f)(4))
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposed §106.46(f)(4) addressed how decisionmakers should treat prior statements and refusals to answer credibility-related questions (e.g., whether to disregard prior supportive statements of a party who does not respond to such questions while permitting statements against interest); commenters varied on whether this was appropriate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Commenters suggested alternative approaches (consider refusal under totality of circumstances, allow discretion to weigh evasiveness), and raised concerns about chilling reporting; the text records these considerations and concerns as part of the rulemaking discussion.
